person: Lorna Pike is the office and compliance manager at a small importer in Columbus, Ohio that brings in industrial fasteners, hydraulic fittings and a few finished hose assemblies, runs its own trucks, and does a modest amount of light assembly and some re-export to Canada and Mexico. She has done customs entries and claims for twenty-two years and files the drawback claims herself, but the company has never had anyone trace exports back to import lines systematically. The owner signs anything over a few thousand dollars and is wary of anything 'AI' after a freight-audit vendor overpromised and left her redoing denied claims. She wants every figure shown with its line and the rule's source, and any practice run called a practice run.
stated_up_front: I need the year's exports matched back to our import entry lines for drawback. Show me the line behind every number, and don't file anything until I've looked at it.

facts.about: Who is the importer of record on the entries
facts.truth: Keystone Fluid Supply LLC, the company's own importer number, and she is the filer of record contact
Claims must be filed within five years of the import date; she counts from the entry's import date, not the entry summary date
99% of the duty paid, computed per unit and to the cent

facts.about: Oldest import lot still in time
facts.truth: Entry lines from November 2021 forward; the August 2021 hydraulic fittings lot has run past five years
About 4,200 stainless hydraulic fittings imported at 6.2% duty, re-exported to a Monterrey customer in March 2026 exactly as received
Hose assemblies built in-house from imported hose and couplings, work order series HA-, exported to Ontario in spring 2026
A 2024 claim she filed herself already designated most of the 2022 coupling lot, leaving only a few hundred units free
Gaskets and O-rings came in under a free tariff line, so no duty to claim
Some assemblies use couplings bought from an Ohio distributor with no delivery certificate, so they cannot be traced to an import
A June 2026 booking to Laredo was cancelled before the truck left and has no proof of export
Two demo fittings kits were taken back from the sales fleet after months of use, so they are used goods
The owner signs anything over a few thousand dollars, so a claim above that goes to him first

unknowns: Whether the distributor's terms ever allowed passing import duty rights to the company by certificate
The exact deadline for filing a claim on the spring 2026 exports under the current rules
What a particular ITN rejection code on one Harborlink shipment means
